nodes.description: ERC20 private mapping _balances tracking token balances per address
ERC20 private nested mapping _allowances storing spender allowances per owner
ERC20 private uint256 _totalSupply holding minted token supply
Electra public constant initialSupply = 16000e18
ERC20.transfer(address,uint256) public virtual override moving tokens from _msgSender()
ERC20.transferFrom(address,address,uint256) public virtual override moving tokens and reducing allowance
ERC20.approve(address,uint256) public virtual override setting spender allowance
ERC20.increaseAllowance(address,uint256) public virtual adding to spender allowance
ERC20.decreaseAllowance(address,uint256) public virtual subtracting from spender allowance
ERC20._transfer(address,address,uint256) internal virtual performing balance updates and Transfer emit
ERC20._mint(address,uint256) internal virtual increasing total supply and account balance
ERC20._approve(address,address,uint256) internal virtual writing allowance mapping
ERC20._burn(address,uint256) internal virtual reducing balance and total supply
Electra constructor minting initialSupply to a hardcoded address
msg.sender accessed through Context._msgSender(), attacker controlled caller address
SafeMath.add arithmetic used for balance and supply increments
SafeMath.sub arithmetic used for balance and allowance decrements
amount parameter of ERC20.transfer
recipient parameter of ERC20.transfer
sender parameter of ERC20.transferFrom
recipient parameter of ERC20.transferFrom
amount parameter of ERC20.transferFrom
spender parameter of ERC20.approve
amount parameter of ERC20.approve
addedValue parameter of ERC20.increaseAllowance
subtractedValue parameter of ERC20.decreaseAllowance
sender parameter of internal _transfer
amount parameter of internal _transfer
account parameter of internal _mint
owner parameter of internal _approve
local variable c holding result of SafeMath.add
local variable c holding result of SafeMath.sub

edges.reason: msg.sender is passed as the from-address into transfer, so the caller controls the source of the token movement
msg.sender is used as the spender in transferFrom allowance check and allowance write
msg.sender becomes the owner whose allowance is set by approve
transfer amount parameter flows into internal _transfer and drives SafeMath.sub/add on balances
recipient parameter flows into internal _transfer balance credit
transferFrom sender parameter flows into internal _transfer as debit account
transferFrom recipient parameter flows into internal _transfer as credit account
transferFrom amount is subtracted from the allowance via SafeMath.sub
spender parameter is written into the allowance mapping by _approve
approve amount is stored as the new allowance value
addedValue is summed into the allowance with SafeMath.add
subtractedValue is subtracted from the allowance with SafeMath.sub
internal _transfer sender is the account debited in _balances
internal _transfer amount is the arithmetic operand for balance add/sub
_mint account receives the newly created balance
_approve owner is the allowance mapping first-level key
transfer delegates state mutation to internal _transfer
transferFrom delegates balance mutation to internal _transfer
transferFrom delegates allowance update to internal _approve
approve delegates allowance writing to internal _approve
increaseAllowance delegates the new allowance write to internal _approve
decreaseAllowance delegates the reduced allowance write to internal _approve
Electra constructor mints the constant initialSupply through internal _mint
initialSupply constant supplies the mint amount in the constructor
internal _transfer subtracts the amount from the sender balance with SafeMath.sub
internal _transfer adds the amount to the recipient balance with SafeMath.add
_mint increases total supply and account balance using SafeMath.add
_burn decrements balance and total supply using SafeMath.sub
local result c of SafeMath.add is returned to the caller
local result c of SafeMath.sub is returned to the caller
SafeMath.add result is written back into the _balances mapping
SafeMath.sub result is written back into the _balances mapping
SafeMath.add result is written into _totalSupply during minting
SafeMath.sub result is written into _totalSupply during burning
_approve writes the amount into the _allowances nested mapping
transferFrom reads the sender allowance from the _allowances mapping
_transfer mutates _balances and then emits Transfer; the _beforeTokenTransfer hook is an extension point that a derived contract could use to make external calls before balance state is settled
_mint calls the _beforeTokenTransfer hook before finalizing balance and supply state, allowing derived-contract callback ordering hazards

normalization_plan.reason: the amount parameter only exists to feed ERC20.transfer into internal _transfer, so it should be folded into the transfer function node
the recipient parameter is a transient argument of ERC20.transfer with no independent semantic identity
the sender parameter belongs solely to ERC20.transferFrom and should be merged into it
the recipient parameter is an argument of ERC20.transferFrom and carries no separate semantics
the transferFrom amount is the arithmetic operand consumed by SafeMath.sub for allowance reduction
the spender parameter is a transient argument of ERC20.approve
the amount parameter is a transient argument of ERC20.approve
addedValue is the operand of the SafeMath.add that computes the new allowance
subtractedValue is the operand of the SafeMath.sub that computes the new allowance
the internal sender argument is only meaningful inside _transfer balance bookkeeping
the internal amount argument is only meaningful inside _transfer balance bookkeeping
the account argument of _mint is consumed directly by the minting routine
the owner argument of _approve is consumed directly by the allowance write
the local c in SafeMath.add is just the returned arithmetic result and can be absorbed into the operation node
the local c in SafeMath.sub is just the returned arithmetic result and can be absorbed into the operation node
